question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: System, Balance, Assessment, Review
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Behavior, Assessment, Response

explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool that helps healthcare workers share critical patient information clearly and concisely during handovers. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main reason a nurse dilutes a medicated lotion?

options.A: To change the color of the cream
options.B: To decrease its active concentration
options.C: To make the container last longer
options.D: To speed up the drying process

explanation: Dilution lowers the percentage of the active drug so it is gentler on sensitive skin. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h1)

question: A male patient says he has noticed sexual changes after starting a new heart medication. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Review his medication list to check for known side effects
options.B: Tell him to stop taking all his heart tablets immediately
options.C: Refer him directly for specialized surgical intervention
options.D: Reassure him that all prescription drugs have zero sexual impact

explanation: Correct! Many heart medications are famous for causing sexual side effects. Checking his drug list is a smart and logical first nursing action.

question: What happens during backward heart failure?

options.A: Blood flows backward right through the skin
options.B: Blood pressure shoots up in the arms
options.C: Fluid backs up into the lungs and body tissues
options.D: The heart stops beating completely for hours

explanation: When the heart can't pump out blood as fast as it receives it, traffic builds up! Fluid backs up behind the weak pump, causing swelling and wet lungs.

question: How do daily community health records help with national health planning in Nigeria?

options.A: They provide data on actual community consumption to help distribute supplies
options.B: They replace the need to conduct national population censuses
options.C: They automatically set the market prices for essential drugs
options.D: They prove to foreign donors that nurses are working hard every day

explanation: Great job thinking big picture! Records from local clinics show ministries how many vaccines and drugs are actually used, helping them send more supplies where needed.

question: Which part of the spinal cord gives rise to the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Lumbar and sacral region
options.B: Craniosacral region
options.C: Thoracolumbar region
options.D: Cervical region only

explanation: Sympathetic fibers emerge from the chest (thoracic) and upper lower-back (lumbar) areas of the spine. That's why we call it the thoracolumbar outflow!

question: When considering a vaginal birth for twins, what position must the first twin be in?

options.A: Footling presentation
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Cephalic presentation

explanation: Great job! A head-first (cephalic) position for the first baby is usually the green light doctors look for before trying a safe vaginal delivery.

question: What does active listening really mean when you are trying to negotiate for health changes?

options.A: Agreeing to all demands without questioning policies
options.B: Understanding the constraints and viewpoints of decision-makers
options.C: Taking notes only to prove the other party is wrong
options.D: Interrupting opponents to correct their facts quickly

explanation: That's right! When you listen to where decision-makers are coming from, it's much easier to find common ground and reach a good compromise.

question: How do medical personnel typically categorize different types of endoscopic examinations?

options.A: By the specific route of access into the body
options.B: By the total cost of the equipment and sterilisation
options.C: By the age and gender of the patient being treated
options.D: By the amount of electrical power the camera uses

explanation: Endoscopies are commonly grouped by whether they enter through natural bodily openings or surgical incisions. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why does a unit manager need to understand both patient advocacy and hospital rules?

options.A: To avoid ever having to care for patients directly
options.B: To replace the hospital director when they are away
options.C: To enforce rules while still protecting patient and staff welfare
options.D: To ensure the hospital makes a profit on every bed

explanation: Spot on! The manager acts like a bridge—they make sure hospital guidelines are followed, but they also stand up to protect the safety and rights of both patients and staff.

question: What do we call it when the bladder bulges into the front wall of the vagina because of weak support?

options.A: Rectocele
options.B: Cystocele
options.C: Urethrocele
options.D: Enterocele

explanation: You're doing great! A cysto-cele happens when the tissue between the bladder and vagina stretches, letting the bladder push forward.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical outcome of a toxic or poor leadership style in nursing?

options.A: Increased nurse absenteeism
options.B: Communication breakdowns
options.C: Improved patient safety culture
options.D: High staff burnout rates

explanation: Poor leadership damages safety culture rather than improving it, leading to errors and poor teamwork. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is a major provider-related cause of unnecessary injections?

options.A: Mandatory laws requiring doctors to prescribe injections daily
options.B: A lack of syringes forcing providers to use intravenous routes
options.C: Hospital rules forbidding the use of oral antibiotics
options.D: Gaps in clinical knowledge and misconceptions about drug potency

explanation: When providers lack proper training, they may mistakenly believe injections are always superior to oral medications. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h3)

question: Which Nigerian agency works closely with the Ministry of Health to regulate and oversee drug standards?

options.A: NEMA
options.B: EFCC
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: JAMB

explanation: You know this! NAFDAC is our frontline agency in Nigeria keeping fake and unsafe drugs away from our people.

question: How do bedside nurses play a direct role in improving healthcare quality?

options.A: By conducting all hospital building maintenance and equipment repairs
options.B: By rewriting all state healthcare laws and national medical policies
options.C: By managing the financial investments and budget allocations of the hospital
options.D: By participating in safety committees and suggesting workflow redesigns

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses work hands-on with daily systems, their practical ideas are gold for creating safer workflows and better patient care.

question: What does the term 'unmet need for family planning' actually mean?

options.A: Doctors refusing to prescribe medicines to married couples
options.B: The total absence of hospitals in a given region
options.C: Willingness to avoid pregnancy without using modern contraception
options.D: A complete ban on all contraceptive drugs by the government

explanation: An 'unmet need' simply describes women who want to delay or stop having children, but aren't currently using any modern birth control method—often due to lack of access or information.

question: What time of day is best for taking a patient's daily weight to get a reliable comparison?

options.A: Immediately after a large dinner
options.B: Late in the evening before sleep
options.C: In the morning after voiding
options.D: Right after finishing afternoon tea

explanation: Weighing in the morning after the bladder is emptied helps avoid the changes in weight caused by food and fluids taken throughout the day.

question: You are posted to a rural village where women have closely spaced pregnancies. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise community leaders to ban all marriages for young women
options.B: Wait for patients to visit the hospital before discussing reproductive health
options.C: Organize community education on birth spacing and offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus all clinic resources exclusively on geriatric care programs

explanation: Fantastic! Taking education directly to the community helps families learn about safe birth spacing and maternal health.

question: How do catabolic pathways supply energy for your cells?

options.A: By combining water molecules with basic salts in the stomach
options.B: By converting excess vitamins directly into electrical impulses
options.C: By breaking down complex molecules to release stored energy
options.D: By forcing simple minerals to absorb sunlight through the skin

explanation: Catabolism is the breaker! It tears down large molecules into smaller pieces, releasing the energy that was trapped inside their chemical bonds so your body can use it.

question: Which viral infection is known as the main cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Hepatitis B Virus
options.B: Human Papillomavirus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Herpes Simplex Virus

explanation: Yes! High-risk strains of HPV are strongly linked to almost all cervical cancer cases. Keeping safe is key!

question: Which of these is a common reason a patient with infective endocarditis might need surgical valve replacement?

options.A: Temporary joint pain in the lower extremities
options.B: Heart failure caused by severe valve damage
options.C: A slight elevation in white blood cell count
options.D: Mild fatigue during routine daily activities

explanation: When an infection destroys the heart valves so badly that the heart starts failing or fluid overloads the body, surgery becomes necessary to fix or replace the valve.

question: In the labor ward, which practice is most important for preventing puerperal sepsis?

options.A: Strict aseptic technique during vaginal examinations
options.B: Restricting oral food intake throughout the first stage of labor
options.C: Administering intravenous fluids to every laboring woman
options.D: Encouraging early ambulation immediately after delivery

explanation: Puerperal sepsis is an infection caused by bacteria entering the reproductive tract. Using clean delivery practices and proper hand hygiene is your best defense as a midwife and nurse!

question: Why do nursing leaders view workplace conflict as a neutral event rather than something purely bad?

options.A: Because hospital management rarely pays attention to small arguments
options.B: Because patient outcomes are never affected by staff disagreements
options.C: Because it simply signals that current dynamics need attention
options.D: Because it always leads to immediate staff resignation

explanation: Think of conflict like a warning light on a car dash. It's not automatically a disaster; it just tells you that some team dynamics need a closer look and a bit of care.

question: At what angle should you give a standard subcutaneous (SC) injection?

options.A: 90 degrees
options.B: 180 degrees
options.C: 45 degrees
options.D: 15 degrees

explanation: A 45-degree angle places the vaccine right into the fatty layer just beneath the skin where it belongs.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge to population policy implementation in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural and religious beliefs favoring large family sizes
options.B: Universal access to fully funded and equipped rural clinics
options.C: Inadequate funding and poor health infrastructure
options.D: Political instability and shifting government priorities

explanation: Sadly, fully funded and equipped rural clinics are far from universal in Nigeria! Most rural clinics actually struggle with shortages, making this option the false statement.

question: Why is checking the suction apparatus considered a critical step before beginning the intubation procedure?

options.A: To inflate the balloon cuff once the tube is in the trachea
options.B: To quickly clear vomit, blood, or secretions blocking the view
options.C: To measure the exact volume of air inside the patient's lungs
options.D: To deliver humidified oxygen straight down the breathing tube

explanation: Unforeseen fluids can instantly obscure the clinician's view of the vocal cords, making immediate suction essential for patient safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: As a nurse, why is the subcutaneous layer (hypodermis) often chosen for giving certain injections?

options.A: It contains large blood vessels for steady drug absorption.
options.B: It prevents medications from entering the systemic circulation.
options.C: It lacks nerve endings, making injections completely painless.
options.D: It consists of hard bone that stabilizes the needle.

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! The hypodermis has a great blood supply, which allows injected medications to absorb smoothly and reliably into the bloodstream.

question: A female client reports a thick vaginal discharge and spotting after intercourse. Which condition should you suspect first as a nurse?

options.A: Ovarian cysts
options.B: Uterine fibroids
options.C: Cervicitis
options.D: Cystitis

explanation: Unusual discharge paired with bleeding after sex are classic clues pointing right to cervical inflammation.

question: A cook slices raw beef and immediately uses the same unwashed knife to cut fresh tomatoes. What just happened?

options.A: Improper freezing
options.B: Thermal abuse
options.C: Cross-contamination
options.D: Food adulteration

explanation: Correct! Using the same knife without washing it transfers bacteria directly from the raw meat into the fresh veggies.

question: Why do modern nurse leaders typically combine several management theories instead of using just one?

options.A: All management theories teach the exact same identical concepts
options.B: Hospital accreditation bodies force leaders to memorize all theories
options.C: Healthcare environments are complex and require varied strategies
options.D: It is illegal in most countries to practice only one leadership style

explanation: Because healthcare mixes strict safety rules with human emotions and shifting emergencies, leaders must adapt and mix theories. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Once a fat-soluble hormone gets inside a target cell, what is its main task?

options.A: Activate membrane-bound adenylate cyclase directly
options.B: Release calcium stores from the cell membrane
options.C: Regulate gene expression and protein synthesis
options.D: Block electrical impulses from the nervous system

explanation: Fat-soluble hormones go straight to the control center (the nucleus) to interact with DNA, turning specific genes on or off to make new proteins. You're crushing these physiology concepts!

question: How do electronic health records support tele-nursing practice?

options.A: By automatically generating prescriptions without a doctor
options.B: By providing distant nurses with quick access to past patient history
options.C: By allowing patients to perform their own laboratory blood tests
options.D: By replacing the need for any direct verbal communication

explanation: Digital records ensure that nurses caring for patients from afar can easily review previous medical notes and treatments. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for drying a newborn immediately after birth?

options.A: To stimulate the baby to cry louder
options.B: To check for birth marks on the skin
options.C: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia
options.D: To remove excess vernix completely

explanation: Wet skin combined with evaporation causes rapid heat loss in newborns, making immediate drying essential to prevent cold stress. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h7)

question: When caring for patients managing injections at home, what is a key duty for the nurse?

options.A: Disposing of patient sharps in regular household garbage bags
options.B: Instructing relatives to reuse syringes if they look clean
options.C: Teaching patients and families safe administration and disposal methods
options.D: Leaving used needles uncapped on the kitchen table for easy access

explanation: Great job! Educating patients and their families prevents accidental needle pricks in homes and communities after they leave the hospital.

question: What is the primary cause of constipation and heartburn during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of digestive enzyme production in the stomach
options.B: Rapid over-activity of the bowel wall muscles
options.C: Relaxation of smooth muscle caused by elevated progesterone
options.D: Direct compression of the liver by the growing fetus

explanation: Progesterone slows down peristalsis throughout the gastrointestinal tract and relaxes the sphincter separating the stomach from the esophagus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: What is the main goal of getting informed consent before doing an implant procedure?

options.A: Proving that the client has paid all required hospital user fees in advance
options.B: Ensuring the client understands the procedure, side effects, and her right to remove the device
options.C: Giving the doctor permission to perform major abdominal surgery if needed
options.D: Protecting the hospital legal team from paying compensation if the client gets pregnant

explanation: Informed consent is all about respect and clear communication, making sure the client willingly agrees because she fully understands what to expect.

question: Why was the team nursing model originally introduced in healthcare settings?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for registered nurses
options.B: To cope with nursing shortages and use various staff skills efficiently
options.C: To make patients pay less money for hospital admission
options.D: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Team nursing was designed to make the best use of available hands when professional nurses are limited in number. It's all about smart teamwork!

question: Which of these details must you include when charting AROM exercises?

options.A: The personal phone number of the patient's family
options.B: The brand name of the bed sheets used in the room
options.C: The specific joints exercised and the number of repetitions
options.D: The exact cost of the physical therapy equipment

explanation: Good documentation means noting down exactly which joints you worked on and how many times they moved.

question: Why is taking leftover antibiotics a bad idea when you catch a common cold?

options.A: Colds require heavy surgical intervention instead of drug therapy
options.B: Cold viruses are already completely immune to all human medicines
options.C: Antibiotics change into sweet syrups when exposed to cold air
options.D: Colds are caused by viruses, whereas antibiotics only target bacteria

explanation: Remember: antibiotics fight bacteria, not viruses. Taking them for a viral cold does zero good and only helps build resistance.

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'gravidity' mean?

options.A: The number of surgical deliveries performed
options.B: The total number of times a woman has been pregnant
options.C: The number of children currently living at home
options.D: The total weight of all babies delivered

explanation: Think of gravidity as the pregnancy counter! It counts every single time a woman has been pregnant, no matter how the pregnancy ended.

question: Why is it smart to check that gas is actually flowing out of the cannula prongs before placing them on the patient?

options.A: To measure the exact oxygen percentage in the room air
options.B: To confirm the equipment works and gas is actively delivering
options.C: To clear out any trapped dust from the manufacturing factory
options.D: To warm up the cold gas before it touches the sensitive nasal lining

explanation: A quick check saves a lot of trouble—you want to make sure there isn't a kinked tube or a closed valve blocking air before it reaches your patient.

question: A patient is admitted with severe dehydration and vomiting, showing signs of early shock. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Restrict oral and intravenous fluids to rest the kidneys
options.B: Administer beta-blockers to slow down the fast heart rate
options.C: Start large-bore IV access and begin rapid fluid replacement
options.D: Keep the patient flat on their back with legs hanging down

explanation: Replacing lost volume quickly using large-bore IV lines is the primary lifesaving intervention for hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of 'controlling' in healthcare management?

options.A: Hiring new nursing graduates for vacancies
options.B: Monitoring performance to ensure care matches established standards
options.C: Assigning daily cleaning duties to support staff
options.D: Creating the holiday duty roster

explanation: Controlling means checking how things are going so you can maintain high standards of patient care.

question: Which vaccine is given in adolescent health programs to protect against cervical cancer later in life?

options.A: Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine
options.B: Oral polio vaccine
options.C: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid vaccine

explanation: Exactly! Giving the HPV vaccine to adolescents is a powerful preventive tool against the strains of the virus that cause cervical cancer.

question: Why are the spaces (sutures) between the baby's skull bones so important during labour?

options.A: They lock the head in a fixed position to stop accidental rotation.
options.B: They supply oxygen directly to the developing foetal brain tissue.
options.C: They prevent any fluid from entering the cranial vault during birth.
options.D: They allow the skull bones to overlap and reduce the head size.

explanation: Those little gaps act like expansion joints! They let the skull bones slide over each other slightly, making the head a bit smaller so it can fit smoothly through the pelvis.

question: A community nurse is inspecting a pregnant woman's home delivery kit. Which item is UNNECESSARY or unsafe for newborn cord care?

options.A: A clean, sterile razor blade for cutting the cord
options.B: Traditional herbal mixture applied directly to the cut cord
options.C: Clean thread to tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.D: Soap and clean water for thorough handwashing

explanation: Applying unsterile substances like herbal mixtures to the umbilical cord introduces bacteria and causes severe neonatal infections like tetanus. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: When are transmission-based precautions added to patient care?

options.A: Only after laboratory tests prove the patient is cured
options.B: When the hospital runs out of standard gloves
options.C: When a specific contagious disease is suspected or confirmed
options.D: Whenever a visitor enters the isolation room

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are extra steps added on top of standard rules when dealing with specific, easily spread germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why do some struggling families in crisis zones resort to early and forced marriage?

options.A: To comply with international nursing association guidelines
options.B: To gain immediate admission into secure university programs
options.C: As a desperate coping strategy to reduce household mouths to feed
options.D: To qualify for free public transportation out of the conflict zone

explanation: Severe economic hardship sometimes pushes desperate parents to marry off young daughters early, hoping to lessen their financial burden.

question: How does a patient's desperate desire to recover quickly affect their injection choices?

options.A: It causes them to demand extra laboratory testing first
options.B: It drives them to refuse all forms of parenteral therapy
options.C: It makes them prioritize fast relief over questioning safety practices
options.D: It encourages them to thoroughly inspect every single medical package

explanation: Spot on! When someone just wants to get well and get back to their daily hustle, safety checks take a back seat.

question: Why is building trust with community leaders so important for a public health nurse?

options.A: It helps ensure that community members accept and participate in prevention programs
options.B: It eliminates the need to collect health data from individual families
options.C: It guarantees that the nurse will receive financial bonuses from the government
options.D: It allows the nurse to bypass standard medical regulations and protocols

explanation: People listen to leaders they trust. When community leaders back your health programs, the local residents will be much more eager to join in!

question: How does a hiatus hernia make acid reflux worse?

options.A: It disrupts the closing ability of the lower sphincter
options.B: It blocks food from entering the small intestine
options.C: It inflames the lining of the large bowel
options.D: It causes the stomach to produce extra acid daily

explanation: When part of the stomach pushes up through the diaphragm, it messes with the natural pressure barrier that normally keeps food and acid safely locked in the stomach.

question: During which stage of an infection does a patient feel just a bit 'off' with vague, mild symptoms, yet they easily spread the illness to others because they're still walking around?

options.A: Illness stage
options.B: Incubation period
options.C: Prodromal stage
options.D: Convalescent period

explanation: Spot on! The prodromal stage is tricky because the patient just feels mildly tired or scratchy-throated, so they keep moving about and unknowingly share germs with everyone.

question: A patient with an undetectable viral load for over a year asks if they can still pass the virus sexually. What is the best response?

options.A: Transmission can only happen if they stop eating fresh fruits
options.B: They can only transmit the virus during the rainy season
options.C: Transmission is still just as likely as before starting treatment
options.D: The risk of sexual transmission is effectively zero as long as adherence is maintained

explanation: Brilliant! This is what we call U=U (Undetectable equals Untransmittable). When a patient takes their meds and stays undetectable, they cannot pass the virus sexually.

question: What is a major environmental factor that increases mosquito breeding and malaria transmission?

options.A: High altitude mountain air with low oxygen levels
options.B: Dense forest canopies blocking all sunlight
options.C: Cool, dry winds blowing during the harmattan season
options.D: Stagnant pools of water after heavy rainfall

explanation: Female mosquitoes lay their eggs in standing water, making puddles and poorly drained areas primary breeding sites after rain. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h4)

question: What is an aortic aneurysm?

options.A: A complete blockage of a vein by a clot
options.B: An abnormal ballooning or weak bulge in the wall of an artery
options.C: A sudden cramp in the heart arteries during stress
options.D: Inflammation of the surface veins in the calf

explanation: An aneurysm happens when a weak spot in a major artery wall starts to stretch and balloon outward, kind of like a weak spot on an old bicycle inner tube.

question: Why should a patient be instructed not to scratch or scrub a tuberculosis skin test site?

options.A: It can irritate the skin and cause false readings.
options.B: It forces the medication to enter the bloodstream instantly.
options.C: It causes the needle mark to bleed heavily.
options.D: It washes away the skin pigment permanently.

explanation: Scratched or irritated skin can cause swelling and redness that mimics a positive immune response, leading to misdiagnosis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: A nurse held two town hall meetings and shared 500 flyers about clean water. To see if the advocacy actually worked (the outcome), what should the nurse check next?

options.A: How many total hours the nurse spent walking to the meeting venues
options.B: How boxes of leaflets were left over in the clinic storage room
options.C: Whether the printer charged a fair market price for the paper used
options.D: Whether the local government committed funds to fix the water source

explanation: You've got it! Handing out flyers is just the activity; seeing if the government actually takes action tells you if your advocacy made a real-world difference.

question: What is the main surgical option used to treat severe stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Widening the urethral opening with a stent
options.B: Placing a supportive sling under the urethra
options.C: Implanting an artificial kidney to filter urine
options.D: Removing the lower portion of the bladder

explanation: A surgical sling acts like a little hammock or seatbelt underneath the urethra to keep it from dropping when you move.

question: Which main chemical messenger in the brain do most sedative drugs target to slow things down?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Gamma-aminobutyric acid
options.C: Norepinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) is the body's natural brake pedal. Sedatives step on this pedal to help calm brain activity. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why do teenage boys and girls need different nutritional care during puberty?

options.A: Girls stop growing in height much earlier than boys do.
options.B: Boys develop more lean muscle while girls accumulate more body fat.
options.C: Girls require virtually no extra protein during puberty.
options.D: Boys have higher vitamin requirements than any other demographic.

explanation: That's correct! Puberty hormones push boys to build more muscle and bone, while girls naturally store a bit more body fat to support future reproductive needs.

question: During continuous bladder irrigation, which finding means you need to take action right away?

options.A: Mild lower abdominal cramping associated with bladder spasms
options.B: Light pink, clear fluid flowing steadily into the collection bag
options.C: Sudden dark red output with large clots and absent drainage
options.D: Clear yellowish urine mixing slowly with the incoming irrigation fluid

explanation: If fluid is going in but not coming out, and the tubing looks blocked with dark clots, the catheter is obstructed! You need to act fast to prevent bladder damage.

question: What are the three main parts of the brain stem, arranged from top to bottom?

options.A: Pons, medulla oblongata, and spinal cord
options.B: Cerebrum, cerebellum, and spinal cord
options.C: Midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata
options.D: Thalamus, hypothalamus, and midbrain

explanation: Think of the brain stem in three neat sections: the midbrain sits up top, the pons is right in the middle, and the medulla oblongata is at the bottom leading right into the spinal cord. You've got this!

question: Where do community health nurses usually first notice unusual patterns of disease?

options.A: During routine home visits, school check-ups, or clinic duties
options.B: While managing hospital kitchen menus and supply inventories
options.C: During international travel conferences held in capital cities
options.D: While reviewing global financial market reports in an office

explanation: Nurses encounter patients directly in communities and clinics, making them the primary observers of local health changes. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the immediate first-aid step after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the puncture wound hard to force blood out
options.B: Soak the affected finger in undiluted bleach
options.C: Wash the site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Apply a strong iodine solution and cover it tightly

explanation: Washing with soap and water immediately helps remove contaminants before they enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h6)

question: What crucial advice should a nurse give a patient taking antibiotics for endometritis?

options.A: Take the pills only when pelvic pain becomes severe
options.B: Double the dose if a single pill is accidentally missed
options.C: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms improve
options.D: Stop taking the medication as soon as the fever drops

explanation: Always remind patients to finish their drugs! Stopping early lets the strongest surviving bacteria bounce back, causing a relapse or drug resistance.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with a surgical wound. Which finding suggests the local inflammation is worsening into a serious infection?

options.A: A slight drop in blood pressure after getting out of bed
options.B: Mild itching directly over the healing scar line
options.C: Normal skin color surrounding the closed surgical staples
options.D: Pus drainage and spreading redness around the incision

explanation: Purulent drainage and expanding erythema are classic clinical indicators of worsening infection in a wound. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the modern medical approach to non-urgent surgeries on intersex infants?

options.A: Delaying non-urgent procedures to protect bodily autonomy until the child can participate
options.B: Mandating hormone therapy immediately after birth
options.C: Ignoring the physical variation completely without any documentation
options.D: Performing immediate surgery on every infant to fix chromosomal imbalances

explanation: You got it! Modern medical ethics value a child's right to their own body, avoiding rushed, irreversible cosmetic surgeries.

question: What is a major nursing priority during the immediate postoperative period following a gynecological surgery?

options.A: Discontinuing all pain medication immediately
options.B: Removing surgical dressings within the first hour
options.C: Monitoring vital signs for signs of hemorrhage
options.D: Initiating rigorous high-intensity aerobic exercise

explanation: Vascular pelvic tissues carry a high risk of bleeding post-surgery, making vital sign monitoring critical to catch hemorrhage early. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)
