options.B: Standard chest radiograph
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.D: Electrocardiogram

explanation: MRI provides excellent soft tissue and bone marrow detail, making it the most sensitive imaging method for early-stage osteomyelitis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h6)

question: How should a nurse document what a patient says about experiencing abuse?

options.A: Write a generalized summary to protect family privacy
options.B: Use direct quotes from the patient and record objective physical findings
options.C: Leave the information out of the chart to prevent legal complications
options.D: Record only the nursing diagnosis without patient comments

explanation: Clear and factual is best! Using direct quotes and objective notes protects the patient and builds a reliable record for future care or legal needs.

question: What does 'family food security' mean?

options.A: Having a locked storage room to protect food from insects
options.B: Having reliable access to enough safe, healthy food for everyone
options.C: Eating meals at the exact same time every single day
options.D: Growing all the family food on a private farm without buying anything

explanation: Food security simply means the household consistently has enough safe and nutritious food to live a healthy, active life.

question: How do you usually arrange the top covers on an admission bed?

options.A: Tucked tightly all around to keep the mattress completely warm
options.B: Folded or fan-folded to the side to allow easy patient transfer
options.C: Arranged in a tight roll directly down the middle of the mattress
options.D: Removed entirely and stored in the ward linen cupboard

explanation: Correct! Folding the top covers to the side means an incoming patient can slip straight into bed without struggling with heavy blankets.

question: When giving ear drops to an adult, how should you pull the ear pinna?

options.A: Downward and forward
options.B: Downward and backward
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Upward and backward

explanation: Great clinical technique! For adults, pulling the pinna upward and backward straightens out that curvy ear canal so your drops flow smoothly down to the eardrum.

question: Which lab tests are most important when starting a patient on an antipsychotic known for metabolic side effects?

options.A: Direct measurement of brain wave activity
options.B: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
options.C: Routine throat swab for bacterial culture
options.D: Complete stool analysis for parasites

explanation: Correct! Because these drugs can disrupt blood sugar and fats, keeping an eye on glucose and lipid levels is essential.

question: If you notice that a broken borehole is causing waterborne illnesses, what role are you mainly playing?

options.A: Hospital administrator
options.B: Surgical assistant
options.C: Needs assessor
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Spot on! Spotting a health issue and tracing it back to environmental problems is what a needs assessment is all about.

question: Which lab test is best for checking the body's stored iron over time?

options.A: Serum ferritin
options.B: Total white cell count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Serum sodium

explanation: Serum ferritin measures the iron tucked away in your body's savings account (stores), making it the top choice for tracking true iron recovery.

question: A family asks to perform a special prayer ritual at the bedside that slightly changes the visiting routine. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the family they must perform their prayers outside the building
options.B: Refuse the request immediately to avoid breaking hospital rules
options.C: Ignore the family and proceed with normal nursing tasks
options.D: Accommodate the request respectfully and find a safe compromise

explanation: As long as it's safe, always respect cultural and spiritual wishes—it's a vital part of compassionate end-of-life care.

question: What should always be done before going to the market to buy food?

options.A: Buy all items in bulk quantities
options.B: Select the most expensive brands
options.C: Wait for foods to start spoiling
options.D: Create a planned menu and budget

explanation: Having a menu and budget prevents impulse buying and ensures you only purchase what is necessary and affordable. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h2)

question: What is the main difference between curative treatment and palliative care?

options.A: Curative treatment aims to eradicate disease, while palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life.
options.B: Curative treatment is only for the elderly, while palliative care is for young children.
options.C: Curative treatment ignores physical pain, while palliative care focuses only on surgery.
options.D: Curative treatment is provided at home, while palliative care requires an intensive care unit.

explanation: Think of it this way: curative treatment fights the disease itself to get rid of it, while palliative care fights the discomfort and pain so the patient can feel better day-to-day. You've got this!

question: How often should you check the skin where an oxygen mask and its straps rest?

options.A: Only when the patient complains of severe bleeding
options.B: Regularly during routine shifts and care checks
options.C: Only once a week before the patient is discharged
options.D: Never, because oxygen masks do not touch the skin

explanation: Checking the skin often helps you catch early redness and prevents pressure sores from the plastic edges and elastic bands.

question: A patient asks why she needs extra iron when her test shows mild anemia. What is your best reply?

options.A: Your blood volume increases greatly, and iron helps build the extra hemoglobin needed.
options.B: Iron tablets replace the calories you lose from not eating enough protein.
options.C: Iron prevents the baby from developing weak bones and teeth.
options.D: Extra iron is only given to stop morning sickness in the first trimester.

explanation: Because her blood volume stretches so much, the blood gets diluted. Extra iron helps her body build all those extra red blood cells she needs!

question: Why do clinicians love checking serum ferritin during a nutritional check-up?

options.A: It directly measures the body's stored iron reserves.
options.B: It calculates the total volume of circulating blood cells.
options.C: It tracks short-term protein intake over forty-eight hours.
options.D: It measures the exact amount of circulating vitamin C.

explanation: Ferritin gives you a sneak peek at how much iron the body has tucked away safely in reserve, long before actual anemia shows up.

question: When taking off personal protective equipment, which item should you remove first?

options.A: Gloves
options.B: Mask
options.C: Gown
options.D: Goggles

explanation: Gloves are typically the most contaminated item, so removing them first prevents transferring pathogens to other pieces of PPE or your skin. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why do we take a musculoskeletal history before doing a physical exam on a patient?

options.A: To measure the patient's exact bone density accurately
options.B: To provide context for interpreting physical findings safely
options.C: To replace the need for diagnostic blood tests entirely
options.D: To determine the exact surgical procedure required

explanation: Gathering a thorough history first gives you the background story you need to understand what you find during the physical exam. Great job!

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a health project?

options.A: Evaluation happens before the project starts, while monitoring never occurs
options.B: Monitoring is ongoing daily tracking, while evaluation measures overall impact
options.C: Monitoring deals only with money, while evaluation deals only with staff
options.D: Monitoring is done by government officials, while evaluation is illegal

explanation: You nailed it! Monitoring is your daily check-in as things happen, while evaluation looks at the big picture and final results. Easy peasy!

question: What is a very common baby-related issue linked to maternal chronic kidney disease?

options.A: Excessive birth weight
options.B: Fetal bone overgrowth
options.C: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.D: Delayed closure of fontanelles

explanation: Because the placenta gets less nourishment, the baby's growth can slow down inside the womb, leading to low birth weight.

question: How long must continuous seizure activity last to be clinically defined as status epilepticus?

options.A: More than twenty-four hours
options.B: Longer than five minutes
options.C: At least one full hour
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Status epilepticus is defined as a seizure lasting more than five minutes or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why are open-ended questions best when taking a drug history?

options.A: They are much faster to document in the nursing notes
options.B: They stop the patient from talking too much
options.C: They encourage the patient to share detailed, honest information
options.D: They prevent the patient from asking about their hospital bill

explanation: Open-ended questions let patients explain their routines in their own words instead of just saying yes or no. Excellent interviewing tip for the wards!

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended for women after childbirth?

options.A: To strengthen muscles and prevent urinary incontinence
options.B: To increase the total volume of breastmilk produced
options.C: To help tighten abdominal skin after a C-section
options.D: To accelerate the growth of the newborn's bones

explanation: Spot on! Pregnancy and pushing during birth stretch out the pelvic floor. Doing these targeted exercises helps tone those muscles back up and stops bladder leakage issues.

question: Why doesn't full milk production start until after the baby and placenta are delivered?

options.A: The infant's cry is required to wake up the dormant pituitary gland
options.B: The mammary ducts do not form until the exact moment of birth
options.C: Prolactin is entirely absent from the maternal bloodstream until labor
options.D: High pregnancy hormones during gestation block full milk secretion

explanation: Spot on! While pregnant, high levels of estrogen and progesterone act like a block on full milk production. Once the placenta is out, that block is removed!

question: Why must you use a filter needle when drawing medication out of a glass ampoule?

options.A: To catch microscopic glass fragments
options.B: To prevent the plunger from sticking
options.C: To filter out air bubbles in the liquid
options.D: To neutralize chemical impurities

explanation: Snap! Snapping open that glass top creates tiny, invisible glass shards. A filter needle acts like a tiny shield, catching those shards so they never make it into the syringe.

question: What is a key feature of algorithmic standing orders?

options.A: They apply only to surgical procedures performed in tertiary hospitals
options.B: They require the nurse to call a doctor before every single step
options.C: They contain blank spaces for the nurse to write their own drug dosages
options.D: They use decision trees with branching questions to guide clinical choices

explanation: Algorithmic standing orders guide the clinician through a series of sequential questions based on patient findings to arrive at the correct care plan. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why do modern nurses view the stages of grief as flexible guidelines rather than strict rules?

options.A: Individuals move through grief stages in unpredictable ways, often skipping or repeating them
options.B: Patients only experience grief if they are told about the stages beforehand
options.C: The stages apply exclusively to children and never to adult patients
options.D: Theoretical models have been proven completely inaccurate through modern laboratory testing

explanation: You nailed it! Grief isn't a straight line. People heal at their own pace, often jumping back and forth between stages.

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water flow off your arms?

options.A: From the hands down toward the elbows
options.B: Directly off the side of the wrists
options.C: From the forearms up to the palms
options.D: From the elbows up toward the fingertips

explanation: Always let water flow from clean (hands) to less clean (elbows). This prevents dirty water from running back down onto your freshly washed fingers!

question: Why is bone weakened enough to cause a pathological fracture in a patient with chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: The infection turns all the solid bone into liquid fat deposits
options.B: Antibiotic medications dissolve the calcium inside the bone matrix
options.C: Muscles pull so hard on the bone that they snap it in half
options.D: Extensive areas of bone death and destruction compromise the structural integrity

explanation: Areas of necrotic bone and chronic destruction weaken the overall structural framework of the bone, making it prone to breaking under normal stress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Sharp pain located exclusively in the upper right shoulder
options.B: Bilateral lower abdominal and pelvic pain
options.C: Severe itching of the external perineal skin
options.D: Painless swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Since both tubes can be affected, inflammation usually shows up as lower belly or pelvic pain felt on both sides.

question: A patient is having a severe panic attack, breathing fast, and crying out in fear. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Hand the patient a stack of educational pamphlets about panic disorder.
options.B: Stay with the patient and speak in calm, short sentences while guiding their breathing.
options.C: Speak loudly and rapidly to snap the patient out of their panic state.
options.D: Leave the room immediately to give the patient privacy to calm down.

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Your calm presence and steady, simple guidance help anchor a patient when their world feels like it's crashing down.

question: A patient with pneumonia says their chest hurts sharply every time they take a deep breath. What's the most likely reason?

options.A: Sudden spasms of the chest muscles
options.B: Extra pressure inside the right side of the heart
options.C: Inflamed lung linings rubbing against the chest wall
options.D: Irritation of the main breathing tubes in the throat

explanation: That sharp pain is called pleuritic chest pain. It happens when the inflamed outer lining of the lungs (pleura) rubs against the chest wall with every breath.

question: What should a nurse use when counselling a patient who does not speak the local language?

options.A: A noisy hospital hallway speaker
options.B: A complex English pharmacology textbook
options.C: A professional medical interpreter
options.D: A young child visiting the family

explanation: Professional interpreters ensure accurate translation of critical medical concepts while keeping patient information private and secure.

question: Why do people with severe malabsorption often look pale, feel very tired, and bruise easily?

options.A: Bile pigment backs up into the subcutaneous fat tissue and stains the skin
options.B: The liver stops producing red blood cells because the stomach is empty
options.C: Undigested food proteins enter the bloodstream and destroy white blood cells
options.D: Malabsorption prevents proper uptake of vital elements like iron, folate, and fat-soluble vitamins needed for blood health

explanation: Without healthy villi, the body misses out on iron, B12, and vitamin K, which leads directly to anemia and easy bleeding. Brilliant clinical thinking!

question: What is mostly packed inside the grey matter of the spinal cord?

options.A: Myelinated axon tracts
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid reservoirs
options.C: Fibrous connective tissue
options.D: Cell bodies and synapses

explanation: You're doing great. While white matter is mostly nerve fibers running up and down, the grey matter is where the action happens—it's packed with cell bodies and synapses doing the actual thinking and processing.

question: What unit of measurement is typically used when programming an electronic infusion pump?

options.A: Drops per minute (gtt/min)
options.B: Milligrams per minute (mg/min)
options.C: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.D: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)

explanation: Electronic infusion pumps are calibrated to deliver exact volumetric amounts calculated in milliliters per hour. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which family dynamic is most strongly linked to an increased risk of early unprotected sex in teens?

options.A: Poor parental supervision and lack of open communication
options.B: Strict adherence to cultural traditions and religious values
options.C: Frequent family meals and shared household chores
options.D: High levels of parental involvement in school activities

explanation: When parents do not monitor their teens or talk openly about sex, youths lack crucial guidance and are more likely to make risky choices. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which hormone do all standard pregnancy test kits look for in blood or urine?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Human placental lactogen
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: hCG (Human chorionic gonadotropin) is the famous pregnancy hormone released right after a fertilized egg implants. That's what turns the test strip positive!

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about modern contraceptives?

options.A: They cause permanent infertility after stopping use
options.B: They require daily surgical procedures to remain active
options.C: They always cure infectious diseases instantly
options.D: They make hair grow faster all over the body

explanation: A widespread myth is that using birth control makes a woman permanently unable to have children later, which nurses must actively correct. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Why might a doctor order a transvaginal ultrasound instead of a transabdominal one?

options.A: It allows visualization of the entire abdomen including the liver and stomach
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any patient preparation or consent
options.C: It is completely painless and causes zero discomfort for all patients
options.D: It places the transducer closer to the pelvic organs for clearer images

explanation: Spot on! Slipping the probe into the vaginal canal brings it right next to the uterus and ovaries, giving us a much sharper picture than scanning through the tummy wall.

question: Why do dietitians recommend high-fiber complex carbs instead of simple sugars for diabetic patients?

options.A: They stimulate the pancreas to grow new beta cells
options.B: They contain zero calories and cannot be converted into fat
options.C: They slow down digestion and prevent rapid blood sugar spikes
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any diabetes medication

explanation: High-fiber carbs take longer to digest, giving a nice, steady release of energy rather than sending blood sugar through the roof. Brilliant nursing logic!

question: Why might a doctor order a biopsy for a vulval lump in an older adult patient?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of fluid inside the cyst
options.B: To check and make sure the persistent or unusual mass is not cancerous
options.C: To prove that the cyst started from an infected hair follicle
options.D: To help the fluid sac absorb faster on its own

explanation: Any unusual or stubborn lump in older women needs a quick tissue check (biopsy) just to be 100% sure it isn't malignant.

question: Which of these is NOT a basic facility needed for a healthy school environment?

options.A: Clean drinking water
options.B: An Olympic-sized swimming pool
options.C: Functional toilet facilities
options.D: A well-equipped sick bay

explanation: Correct! While a big pool is fun, basic health needs are all about clean water, good toilets, and a clinic space to care for sick students.

question: What is the primary reason why cleaning must happen before sterilization?

options.A: Organic matter protects germs from the sterilization process
options.B: Water makes the instruments softer to handle
options.C: Soap adds a layer of chemical protection
options.D: Washing removes the unpleasant metal smell

explanation: Dried blood and body fluids form a barrier over microorganisms that blocks heat or chemicals from reaching them. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: Which of these phrases is an example of respectful, person-first language in mental health nursing?

options.A: A chronic alcoholic clogging the ward
options.B: A substance abuser who lacks willpower
options.C: A person with a substance use disorder
options.D: A hopeless addict seeking attention

explanation: You nailed it! Person-first language puts the human being before the medical condition, reminding us to treat every patient with dignity and respect.

question: What does patient confidentiality require of you as a nurse?

options.A: To refuse documentation in the official hospital medical record
options.B: To share patient secrets with any interested family member
options.C: To keep patient diagnoses hidden permanently from the care team
options.D: To protect patient health information from unauthorized disclosure

explanation: Correct! Confidentiality means keeping private health info safe and only sharing it with the healthcare team taking care of them.

question: A manager wants to check if nurses are consistently signing off on medication times. Which tool is best for this?

options.A: Staff annual performance reviews
options.B: Patient satisfaction surveys
options.C: Hospital financial balance sheets
options.D: Nursing chart audits

explanation: Checking patient charts and medication sheets directly shows whether documentation rules are being followed on the ward.

question: Why must you always have a transport plan in place before attending a home birth?

options.A: It prevents wasting critical time when a sudden obstetric emergency arises
options.B: It removes the legal liability from the attending family
options.C: It guarantees that transport vehicles will arrive instantly
options.D: It ensures that normal births happen faster

explanation: Emergencies can pop up unexpectedly. Having vehicles and a hospital lined up beforehand means no scrambling or wasting precious minutes.

question: Which chemical released in the body causes the rapid swelling and itching after an insect sting?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Histamine

explanation: Spot on! Venom triggers mast cells to release histamine, which makes local blood vessels open up and leak fluid into the skin, causing swelling and itchiness.

question: What kind of surgery involves removing a healthy organ because a patient has a high genetic risk of getting cancer there later?

options.A: Curative surgery
options.B: Prophylactic surgery
options.C: Diagnostic surgery
options.D: Palliative surgery

explanation: Great thinking! Prophylactic means preventative. Doctors perform this to remove healthy tissue before cancer ever gets a chance to start.

question: Which laboratory test is considered the gold standard for confirming a diagnosis of sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Sickle solubility test
options.B: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.C: Haemoglobin electrophoresis
options.D: Full blood count

explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis separates the different types of haemoglobin proteins to provide a definitive diagnosis of the specific genotype. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: When is it most important to routinely screen women for reproductive infections?

options.A: Whenever routine malaria testing is conducted
options.B: Only after the patient develops severe chronic pelvic pain
options.C: Strictly upon reaching forty years of age
options.D: During the first prenatal visit and for sexually active young adults

explanation: Early screening catches silent infections early, especially during pregnancy or in young adults before any lasting damage is done.

question: How do drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) help treat erectile dysfunction?

options.A: They act as direct agonists on alpha-1 adrenergic receptors
options.B: They increase sympathetic tone to close the venous channels
options.C: They directly stimulate the release of acetylcholine from nerve endings
options.D: They block phosphodiesterase type 5 to preserve cGMP levels

explanation: Brilliant! By blocking the enzyme that breaks down cGMP, these drugs help keep the muscles relaxed and blood flowing smoothly.

question: What is the main purpose of using the 'teach-back' method when educating patients?

options.A: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize pharmacological side effects
options.B: Allowing the patient to teach nursing students about herbal remedies
options.C: Checking whether the patient truly understands how to take their medication
options.D: Evaluating the financial cost of drugs prescribed at discharge

explanation: Well done! Instead of just asking 'do you understand?', teach-back has patients explain the instructions in their own words so you know they've got it.

question: Why must the dropper be aimed away from the center nasal septum during instillation?

options.A: To block the airflow in both nostrils equally
options.B: To avoid injuring the delicate tissues and causing bleeding
options.C: To make sure the liquid enters the mouth directly
options.D: To prevent the dropper tip from bending

explanation: The nasal septum has a fragile blood supply that can easily bleed if scraped by a dropper tip. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h7)

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?

options.A: Pink to brick-red
options.B: Bright yellow or green
options.C: Dark purple to black
options.D: Pale white or gray

explanation: Correct! A healthy stoma is packed with tiny blood vessels, which gives it a nice moist, pink to brick-red color.

question: During a digestive check, which physical sign is best for quickly spotting dehydration?

options.A: Moisture of the oral mucous membranes
options.B: The presence of minor scars on the skin
options.C: The temperature of the lower legs
options.D: The exact color of the client's hair

explanation: Checking inside the mouth! Dry or sticky gums and tongue are quick, reliable signs that a patient is losing too much fluid from vomiting or diarrhea.

question: How does a heavy nurse-to-patient workload negatively impact the implementation of care standards?

options.A: Staff automatically memorize all clinical guidelines much faster
options.B: Patients refuse to let nurses check their vital signs
options.C: Hospital management increases the nurse's monthly salary
options.D: Nurses rush care and may skip important procedural steps due to fatigue

explanation: When overworked, nurses have to prioritize immediate life-saving tasks, leading to skipped protocols and lower compliance. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with orthodox medical practitioners
options.B: To punish communities that fail to follow sanitation guidelines
options.C: To systematically address population health problems using available resources
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in tertiary hospitals

explanation: The planning cycle provides a structured framework for public health nurses to tackle community-wide health issues efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is just treating medical symptoms often not enough for a community?

options.A: Patients refuse to visit primary health care clinics unless accompanied by local leaders
options.B: Environmental and social root causes like poor water or housing will keep causing new illnesses
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for community outbreaks
options.D: Medical treatments are too expensive for the government to maintain long-term

explanation: Spot on! If we treat a patient in the clinic but send them back to drink contaminated water, they'll just fall sick again. We have to fix the environment too!

question: How do patients in strict isolation often feel emotionally?

options.A: Indifference to hospital staff
options.B: Loneliness and anxiety
options.C: Relief from daily visitors
options.D: Excitement about privacy

explanation: Being cut off from normal human contact behind barriers can make patients feel very lonely and worried. Empathy goes a long way here!

question: Why are older adults much more prone to chronic dehydration?

options.A: Kidneys produce excessive water during the night.
options.B: The natural sensation of thirst decreases with age.
options.C: Older adults require zero fluids to maintain normal health.
options.D: The skin absorbs all environmental moisture instantly.

explanation: Spot on! As people grow older, their internal thirst signals get quieter, meaning they might not feel thirsty even when their body is crying out for water.

question: Which finding in a new mother's lochia (postnatal discharge) should worry you the most?

options.A: A foul or offensive odor coming from the discharge
options.B: A slight increase in flow when the mother stands up
options.C: Small dark clots passed during the first three days
options.D: A gradual fading from red to pink over two weeks

explanation: Lochia naturally changes color and has a normal earthy smell, but a foul odor is a major sign of a uterine infection (endometritis) that needs quick treatment.

question: A patient at 32 weeks reports she has not felt her baby move all day. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Mild physiological anemia of pregnancy
options.B: Potential fetal distress or compromise
options.C: Standard weight gain in the third trimester
options.D: Normal resting behavior of a mature fetus

explanation: Whenever a mom says baby's movements have stopped or slowed right down, treat it as an emergency and check the baby right away.

question: What is the primary purpose of using a nasogastric (NG) tube for gastric decompression?

options.A: To remove fluid, gas, and contents from the stomach
options.B: To remove blood collections from inside the chest cavity
options.C: To supply oxygen into the upper airway passages
options.D: To drain excess urine directly from the bladder

explanation: Correct! 'Decompression' just means taking the pressure off. An NG tube sucks out built-up gas and fluid so the stomach can rest and the patient won't vomit.

question: What is the proper clinical term for unusually heavy or long menstrual periods?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Oligomenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Dysmenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia simply means heavy menstrual bleeding. As future nurses, we always watch out for this because it puts patients at risk for anemia.

question: Which Nigerian agency coordinates national policies and responses related to HIV?

options.A: Nigerian Football Federation (NFF)
options.B: Nigerian Broadcasting Commission (NBC)
options.C: Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC)
options.D: National Action Committee on AIDS (NACA)

explanation: NACA is the main body responsible for coordinating the national fight against the HIV epidemic in Nigeria. Great exam fact to lock into your memory!

question: A patient arrives sweating heavily with thick makeup on their forehead. What should you do for their temperature?

options.A: Use the temporal thermometer right over the makeup
options.B: Use another route, like the ear or mouth
options.C: Wipe the forehead with alcohol and read immediately
options.D: Add two degrees to whatever the temporal reading says

explanation: Sweat and cosmetics mess up forehead heat readings. Save yourself a headache and switch to an oral or tympanic route!

question: How does regular exercise help manage high blood pressure over time?

options.A: It replaces the need for kidneys to filter excess body water.
options.B: It blocks cholesterol from entering the bloodstream entirely.
options.C: It reduces systemic vascular resistance and strengthens the heart.
options.D: It permanently thickens the walls of the heart chambers.

explanation: Great job! Staying active helps your heart pump more efficiently and lowers the resistance in your blood vessels.

question: Who among the following is NOT usually in the high-risk group for severe food poisoning?

options.A: Healthy young adult office workers
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Older adults with chronic health conditions
options.D: Pregnant women and their babies

explanation: Exactly! Healthy young adults generally have strong immune systems to fight off food bugs easily. It's the very young, elderly, and pregnant women we worry about most.

question: A family caring for a young adult with a spinal cord injury insists on doing everything for them, refusing to let them try dressing themselves. What is this family showing?

options.A: Harmful overprotection
options.B: Caregiver neglect
options.C: Sibling rivalry
options.D: Professional detachment

explanation: You nailed it! While out of love, doing everything for a patient stops them from building confidence and independence.

question: When should you choose sterile surgical gloves instead of regular exam gloves?

options.A: When performing a procedure inside a sterile body cavity
options.B: During routine physical checks on unbroken skin
options.C: Whenever touching a patient with an infection
options.D: When cleaning up a blood spill on the floor

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile space or use sterile instruments, you need sterile gloves to keep bacteria out. You've got this!

question: Which main muscle forms the wall of the urinary bladder and stretches as it fills up with urine?

options.A: Trigone muscle
options.B: Detrusor muscle
options.C: Dartos muscle
options.D: Cremaster muscle

explanation: You've got this! The detrusor muscle is the big muscular wall of the bladder that stretches out nicely to hold urine until you're ready to go.

question: What is the main job of the lower esophageal sphincter?

options.A: To control how fast water leaves the stomach
options.B: To release digestive enzymes into the upper esophagus
options.C: To grind solid food particles into a liquid mixture
options.D: To prevent stomach acid from flowing back into the esophagus

explanation: This sphincter acts like a one-way gate, closing tightly so harsh stomach juices don't splash up and burn your food pipe. Simple and clear!

question: Which of the following does NOT help build a strong research culture?

options.A: Discouraging nurses from reading studies done by other healthcare professions
options.B: Creating mentorship programs between senior and junior staff
options.C: Establishing local grants to fund small nursing projects
options.D: Providing protected time during work hours for research activities

explanation: Healthcare is team-based! Shutting out studies from other professions hurts teamwork and slows down evidence-based practice. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these common germs needs to hijack a living host cell in order to multiply?

options.A: Virus
options.B: Fungus
options.C: Bacterium
options.D: Parasite

explanation: Think of viruses as tiny freeloaders! They don't have the tools to reproduce on their own, so they must break into a living host cell to multiply.

question: What is the primary purpose of plotting a partograph during labor in a rural clinic?

options.A: To measure the exact birth weight of the newborn infant
options.B: To record the baby's future immunization appointments
options.C: To monitor the progress of labor and detect deviations early
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used to track cervical dilation and fetal condition, helping midwives spot prolonged labor promptly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which hormone is released by the adrenal glands to help raise heart rate and blood pressure during shock?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Adrenaline

explanation: The sympathetic nervous system releases adrenaline and noradrenaline to quickly boost heart rate and tighten blood vessels during a crisis. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the core focus of transactional leadership?

options.A: Giving staff complete independence
options.B: Inspiring a grand shared vision
options.C: Voting on every policy change
options.D: Rewards and punishments for performance

explanation: Transactional leaders use a system of rewards for meeting goals and corrections or punishments for failing to meet them. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient in strict isolation cries because no one wants to touch them without gear. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Assure them that the infection is not serious at all
options.B: Remove your gown and gloves to prove you care
options.C: Tell them the rules are necessary and leave the room quickly
options.D: Acknowledge their feelings and spend time talking calmly with them

explanation: Validating emotions and offering supportive conversation helps reduce the psychological toll of isolation while keeping safety intact. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: Why can giving too much normal saline be harmful to a patient with uncontrolled internal bleeding?

options.A: It lowers the patient's heart rate to dangerous levels
options.B: It causes severe dehydration
options.C: It dilutes essential clotting factors and washes away fragile new clots
options.D: It destroys all existing red blood cells instantly

explanation: Pumping in too much plain IV fluid dilutes the blood's natural clotting proteins, making it harder for the body to stop the bleeding. Balance is key!

question: Why should you avoid checking blood pressure on the arm of a patient who has had lymph nodes removed from that side?

options.A: It causes immediate permanent damage to the brachial artery
options.B: It can impair fluid drainage and trigger severe lymphedema
options.C: The blood pressure reading will always read falsely high
options.D: It stops white blood cells from maturing in the bone marrow

explanation: When lymph nodes are removed, drainage in that limb is already fragile. Squeezing the arm with a blood pressure cuff can back up fluid and cause a painful swelling condition called lymphedema. Good clinical safety knowledge to keep in mind!

question: Which ethical principle refers to the nurse's core duty to do no harm to patients?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Non-maleficence
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Great nursing foundation here! 'Non-maleficence' literally means avoiding any physical, emotional, or psychological harm to the patients in your care.

question: Where should you place the two AED pads on an adult patient's bare chest?

options.A: Center of the chest and middle of the back
options.B: Left side of the ribs and right side of the abdomen
options.C: Both shoulders near the neck collarbones
options.D: Upper right chest and lower left ribcage

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right and the other on the lower left lets the electrical current flow diagonally right through the heart muscle.

question: A mum mentions she is breastfeeding her baby but also giving thin porridge to help the baby sleep through the night. How do you assess this?

options.A: This is a healthy practice that ensures the infant stays full through the night
options.B: This technique prevents maternal exhaustion without affecting the infant
options.C: This practice is mixed feeding and increases the risk of HIV transmission
options.D: This method safely prepares the baby's stomach for solid foods early

explanation: Even though mums want better sleep, adding porridge early counts as mixed feeding and raises transmission risks. Gentle counseling here is key!

question: A patient has had lingering joint swelling for over eight months. What type of inflammation is this?

options.A: Chronic inflammation
options.B: Vascular collapse
options.C: Systemic sepsis
options.D: Acute inflammation

explanation: You got it! When inflammation hangs around for months with continuous immune activity, we call it chronic.

question: How do standard daily contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By permanently blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: By stopping ovulation and changing the cervical mucus
options.C: By killing all bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By neutralizing stomach acid so hormones cannot absorb

explanation: The hormones in the pill do a double-duty job: they tell the body to pause ovulation and make the cervical mucus thick so sperm can't get through.

question: Why is women empowerment considered essential for achieving universal health coverage?

options.A: It stops the government from building more primary health centers
options.B: It allows women to actively participate in seeking and utilizing healthcare services
options.C: It completely removes the financial cost of purchasing hospital drugs
options.D: It guarantees that only female doctors will treat patients

explanation: When women have autonomy, they can freely access health facilities and make prompt decisions that improve community health indices. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: What happens to the arterioles in your muscles when you start heavy exercise?

options.A: They collapse completely to stop bleeding
options.B: They harden permanently to boost pressure
options.C: They dilate to let more blood through
options.D: They constrict to block fast blood flow

explanation: Working muscles need more oxygen, so local arterioles relax and open wide to increase blood supply. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why is taking corticosteroids together with NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) a big risk?

options.A: It causes blood pressure to drop dangerously low.
options.B: It cancels out the steroid so it doesn't work.
options.C: It greatly increases the chance of stomach ulcers and bleeding.
options.D: It stops the liver from filtering other drugs.

explanation: Brilliant! Both drugs irritate the stomach lining. Combining them multiplies the risk of painful ulcers and internal bleeding.

question: Why do pregnant women often experience frequent urination?

options.A: The ascending colon expands
options.B: The abdominal aorta shifts
options.C: The right kidney grows larger
options.D: The urinary bladder gets squeezed

explanation: Spot on! Because the female bladder sits right below the uterus, a growing pregnancy means less room for the bladder to store urine. You'll see this a lot in clinical rotations!

question: A 10-week-old baby is brought for immunizations, but currently has a high fever and a bad cough. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the child straight to surgery for a diagnostic blood test
options.B: Defer the immunizations temporarily until the acute illness resolves
options.C: Administer all scheduled vaccines immediately regardless of the fever
options.D: Permanently ban the child from receiving any future vaccines

explanation: When a child is acutely sick with a high fever, it's wise to hold off (defer) the shots until they feel better so symptoms don't get confused.

question: How should you as a nurse handle a client whose religion forbids modern family planning?

options.A: Refuse to treat them until they accept a method
options.B: Respect their belief while offering supportive, non-judgmental dialogue
options.C: Report their religious leader to the local police
options.D: Argue with them until they change their religious affiliation

explanation: Wonderful! As nurses, we always respect our patients' spiritual beliefs while keeping the health conversation warm and open.

question: Why might doctors order an amniocentesis late in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To treat an active uterine infection
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the growing fetus
options.C: To check if the fetal lungs are mature enough for birth
options.D: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure

explanation: If there's talk of delivering early, a late amniocentesis checks the fluid to see if the baby's lungs are strong and ready to breathe on their own.

question: Why should community midwives collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants outnumber all trained doctors in cities.
options.B: TBAs are often trusted first-line care providers in rural areas.
options.C: TBAs have advanced surgical degrees from university hospitals.
options.D: Government policy requires TBAs to manage major surgical operations.

explanation: Because many women naturally seek out TBAs first, working with them helps redirect high-risk cases to formal health facilities much faster. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: Ten minutes after delivery, a mum starts bleeding heavily and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should you do right away?

options.A: Encourage the mother to walk around the room to boost circulation
options.B: Wait patiently for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Send the patient home immediately with iron tablets
options.D: Perform fundal massage and administer the prescribed uterotonic drug

explanation: Well done! Massaging the uterus helps it contract, and giving the uterotonic medication stops the bleeding fast.

question: What process do the kidneys use to make new sugar during long periods of fasting?

options.A: Lipogenesis
options.B: Glycogenolysis
options.C: Glycolysis
options.D: Gluconeogenesis

explanation: You've got this! When you haven't eaten in a while and need energy, your kidneys can actually build new glucose (gluconeogenesis) to keep your blood sugar stable.

question: What does the presence of thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid usually indicate?

options.A: Rapid dilation of the maternal cervix
options.B: A normal and healthy progression of labour
options.C: Normal kidney function in a full-term baby
options.D: Previous foetal stress and bowel relaxation

explanation: Hypoxia relaxes the foetal anal sphincter, causing the baby to pass meconium into the amniotic fluid before delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h3)

question: In ventilator settings, what does the term PEEP stand for?

options.A: Positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: Primary external air pressure
options.C: Peak elastic expiration pressure
options.D: Pulmonary evaluation and expansion protocol

explanation: PEEP leaves a tiny bit of pressure in the lungs right at the end of a breath. This stops the tiny air sacs from collapsing like deflated balloons!

question: What happens in the brain during a seizure that puts cells at risk of injury?

options.A: Brain tissue instantly freezes due to a sudden halt in all chemical reactions.
options.B: Neurons fire excessively and synchronously, causing a massive spike in metabolic and oxygen demand.
options.C: Inhibitory neurotransmitters multiply rapidly and shut down all electrical signals.
options.D: Blood flow completely stops to every part of the brain simultaneously.

explanation: During a seizure, brain cells fire wildly all at once. They burn through energy and oxygen way faster than the body can supply it.

question: Why do community nurses need to work with other sectors like agriculture and education?

options.A: Hospitals lack the capacity to treat infectious diseases
options.B: Ministries of health cannot function without financial loans
options.C: Health is influenced by many sectors like agriculture and education
options.D: Nurses are required to handle civil engineering tasks

explanation: Think about it—good health depends on food production, clean water, and learning. Teamwork across different fields makes community health possible!

question: What actually happens when someone has a physical dependence on a drug?

options.A: The complete inability to remember recent events after drinking
options.B: A sudden allergy to chemical substances found in prescription drugs
options.C: The body reacts with unpleasant symptoms when the drug is stopped
options.D: An emotional desire to feel happy without taking any medicine

explanation: Spot on! Physical dependence simply means the body has gotten so used to the drug that it protests with withdrawal signs when the supply cuts off. You've got this!

question: What happens during the pre-briefing or preparation phase of a simulation?

options.A: Students clean and store all the equipment used in the simulation
options.B: Students review patient charts, readings, and protocols before the lab
options.C: The entire simulation scenario is acted out for a second time
options.D: The instructor grades the student performance and assigns final marks

explanation: Preparation ensures learners come with the foundational knowledge required to tackle the upcoming clinical scenario. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h4)

question: Where are the descending motor fibers found as they pass through the pons?

options.A: The superior colliculus
options.B: The ventral basilar part
options.C: The middle cerebellar peduncle
options.D: The dorsal tegmentum

explanation: Motor pathways travel right down through the front (ventral or basilar section) of the pons. You're building solid neuro anatomy knowledge!

question: Which of the following describes economic violence in a domestic relationship?

options.A: Splitting utility bills evenly between two working adults
options.B: Forgetting to consult a partner before making a household purchase
options.C: Donating family savings to a charity without asking
options.D: Controlling access to money and preventing a partner from working

explanation: Economic abuse involves financial control, making the survivor entirely dependent on the abuser for survival. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h2)

question: Why is counting needles such an important duty for a nurse?

options.A: It speeds up the surgeon's work during complex procedures
options.B: It serves as a legal and physical safety barrier for the patient
options.C: It is only done to satisfy hospital administrative rules
options.D: It reduces the need to sterilize instruments after the case

explanation: Great job thinking about patient safety! Accurate counts protect your patient from harm and protect you and your team legally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the main job of desmosomes in heart muscle cells?

options.A: Isolating the atria electrically from the lower ventricles
options.B: Holding adjacent muscle cells tightly together during strong contractions
options.C: Producing adenosine triphosphate for resting heart muscle
options.D: Regulating the flow of calcium ions into the cell interior

explanation: Desmosomes act like heavy-duty rivets. When the heart squeezes hard, they keep the cells from pulling apart!

question: Why should a client wash their hair thoroughly before coming in for an EEG?

options.A: To prevent the client from catching a scalp infection
options.B: To make the hair grow faster after the sticky paste is applied
options.C: To remove oils and hair products that block electrode contact
options.D: To cool down the scalp so the metal discs stick better

explanation: Hair gels, oils, and sprays create a barrier that stops the EEG electrodes from making good electrical contact with the scalp. Clean hair makes for a clear test!

question: Why is healthy, unbroken skin considered part of the innate immune system?

options.A: It contains mature T-lymphocytes that destroy foreign organisms
options.B: It acts as a physical barrier that stops pathogens from entering the body
options.C: It actively manufactures specific antibodies against local skin bacteria
options.D: It produces high levels of inflammatory cytokines during minor scrapes

explanation: Spot on! Your skin is your body's first wall of defense, stopping germs from getting inside in the first place.

question: Why do inactivated (killed) vaccines often need multiple booster doses?

options.A: The live virus inside them multiplies too quickly
options.B: The killed organisms produce a weaker immune response than live ones
options.C: They do not contain any antigens to trigger B-cells
options.D: They destroy existing memory cells in the bloodstream

explanation: You nailed it! Since the germs are dead and can't multiply, boosters give our immune system a helpful reminder to keep us protected.

question: Can a person experience wellness even if they have a chronic illness?

options.A: No, chronic illnesses automatically prevent any form of social well-being
options.B: Yes, but only if they completely stop taking all prescribed medications
options.C: No, because wellness requires the total absence of any medical diagnosis
options.D: Yes, by effectively managing their condition and maintaining a positive outlook

explanation: Exactly! Having a chronic condition doesn't mean you can't live a full, happy life with proper self-care and a good mindset.

question: Why are progestin-only implants safer for women with a history of blood clots compared to combined oral pills?

options.A: They actively dissolve existing blood clots within the deep veins
options.B: They completely destroy all circulating red blood cells in the body
options.C: They bypass the liver entirely and go straight into the heart muscle
options.D: They do not contain estrogen, which is the main hormone linked to clotting risks

explanation: Estrogen is usually the troublemaker when it comes to blood clots in contraceptives. Since implants are progestin-only, they leave estrogen out of the picture!

question: What are you comparing when you perform a 'gap analysis' in community health?

options.A: The age of children versus the age of their grandparents
options.B: Current health status against desired health standards
options.C: The salary of nurses versus doctors in the clinic
options.D: Total population size against total land area in kilometers

explanation: A gap analysis simply looks at the gap between where the community's health is right now and the healthy standard we want them to achieve.
